chunks: Muḥammad al-Ḥalabī asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a group of people: does a cow suffice for them? He said:
"As for the hady, no. But as for the uḍḥiyah, yes. And the hady suffices in place of the uḍḥiyah."

key_terms.الْأَضْحَى: the ritual sacrifice of Eid al-Aḍḥā
key_terms.الْأُضْحِيَّةِ: the sacrificial animal offered as uḍḥiyah
key_terms.الْبَقَرَةُ: a cow used as the sacrificial animal
key_terms.الْهَدْيِ: the sacrificial offering associated with hajj rites

ai.seo_question: Does one cow suffice for a group in hady and uḍḥiyah according to Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal distinction between the hady offered in hajj and the uḍḥiyah sacrifice. It states that a cow does not suffice for a group in hady, but it does suffice for them in uḍḥiyah, and that hady also fulfills the place of uḍḥiyah.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3067 - Muhammad al-Halabi asked Abu Abdullah (as) about a group of people—does a cow suffice for them?
Imam (as) replied: "As for the hady (sacrificial offering for Hajj), no. But as for the sacrifice (Udhiyah), yes. And the hady suffices in place of the sacrifice."
